Screened five Texas coastal/new-trail candidates across the new Palacios TPWD trail family and Powderhorn Coloma Creek. No route was added because all candidates failed the current PaddleToday scored-river live-condition and numeric-threshold model, with additional route-shape, open-bay, wind/tide, shipping-channel, camping, and limited-shoreline-access blockers.

candidatesScreened.blocker: TPWD supports the new 10-mile one-way Tres Palacios River Trail from Carl Park Boat Ramp to East Bay Park with public access coordinates and notes limited camping at Carl Park and no camping at East Bay Park. USGS 08162600 was product-live at 38.1 cfs / 3.70 ft at 2026-08-12 07:30 CDT, but the selected route widens into Tres Palacios Bay and TPWD frames suitability around water level, tide, flow, and wind without publishing numeric cfs/stage thresholds. No accepted coastal/tidal route-scoring model exists for this river-to-bay transition, so the candidate fails threshold/live-condition policy before implementation.

TPWD supports the 1.5-mile one-way City by the Sea Trail between East Bay Park and South Bay Park with public access coordinates and no-camping statements at both parks. The trail follows the Palacios seawall through bay water and TPWD frames travel time around water levels, tide, flow rate, and wind. No product-supported live river gauge or accepted numeric coastal/tidal threshold model surfaced, so it cannot be scored as a PaddleToday river route.

TPWD supports the 2-mile roundtrip Palacios Wetlands Trail from East Bay Park into coastal salt marsh and wetland habitat, including a humpback bridge, a second lower bridge that may need portage in higher water, and a turn-around at the Highway 35 culvert. It is a same-access roundtrip marsh route, not a downstream point-to-point river reach, and no supported live condition adapter or numeric threshold model surfaced.

TPWD supports the 6-mile one-way Dolphin Run Trail from South Bay Park to Jensen Point with public access coordinates, but it crosses the Palacios shipping channel, rounds a private peninsula, and then crosses open Turtle Bay where TPWD warns strong winds and choppy water can occur. No product-supported live river gauge or accepted numeric wind/tide/bay threshold model surfaced, so the safety and condition gates fail before implementation.

TPWD supports Powderhorn as a four-trail shoreline/marsh system and lists the Coloma Creek Trail as an 8-mile roundtrip from the FM 1289 bridge, but says the creek behaves more like shallow bay water, includes mostly shallow mud flats, and is part of a coastal route-choice family with wind, tide, and access caveats. No product-supported live gauge or accepted numeric condition threshold model surfaced, so the route cannot be scored under the current river-route policy.
